newsitem.title: USA: First Union to buy Signet for $3.25 bln.
newsitem.headline: First Union to buy Signet for $3.25 bln.

text.p: First Union Corp has agreed to acquire Signet Banking Corp in a stock swap worth $3.25 billion, the banks said Monday.
First Union, the sixth largest U.S. bank, will exchange 0.55 share of its common stock for each share of Signet, valuing Signet at about $53.59 a share.
Signet closed at 36-11/16 on Friday. First Union finished at 97-7/16.
Reflecting First Union's previously announced two-for-one stock split payable on July 31, the exchange ratio will be 1.10 First Union shares for each Signet share.
The companies expect the merger, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, to close by December 31.
First Union said it expects the merger will have a positive impact on earnings per share in 1998, and an increasingly positive impact in 1999 and beyond.

First Union said these expectations are based on estimated savings of 50 percent of Signet's annual expenses, or $242 million, as well as incremental revenue growth of $37 million as First Union brings its financial products and services to Signet customers.
The conversion of Signet's operating systems is expected to take only four months.
First Union said it expects to take an after-tax merger restructuring charge of $135 million in 1997.
Following the merger, Signet Chairman and Chief Executive Malcolm McDonald will become CEO of First Union's Virginia, Maryland and Washington region.
Benjamin Jenkins III, current president of First Union's operations in the region, will become chief operating officer.
In connection with the merger agreement, Signet has granted First Union an option to buy, under certain circumstances, up to 19.9 percent of Signet's outstanding common stock.

At consummation of the merger, First Union will rescind its existing authorization to buy back stock, which authorized the repurchase of up to 25 million shares (or 50 million, adjusted for the stock split).
During 1997, First Union has repurchased about 11 million shares under the authorization (about 22 million on a post-split basis).
First Union said it will have assets of about $155 billion when the merger is completed.
